answer: Cross-epoch footprint matching. Each identity must reproduce its prior activity fingerprint—response latency profile, tool-call mix, and a signed sonnet of routine logs—within tolerance at every epoch boundary. A cluster sharing one operator stays correlated and gets pruned when correlation dips below the nadir threshold on the scoring knoll. An attacker must rebuild distinct, stable behaviour per identity across epochs, costing a sustained per-identity maintenance budget in compute and unique activity, not one upfront payment.
